bib.title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

read.skipped: Reference list and figure-only pages skimmed

question: Can transformers synthesize high-resolution images if a CNN first learns a compact, context-rich discrete codebook of image constituents?
hypothesis: Low-level image structure is well described by local (convolutional) connectivity while global composition needs transformers, so combining a CNN codebook with a transformer is efficient and expressive.
contributions: VQGAN: a convolutional VQVAE variant with perceptual and patch-adversarial losses giving a context-rich codebook at high compression
Autoregressive transformer over codebook indices with sliding-window sampling for megapixel images
A single approach for conditional synthesis (class, segmentation, depth, edges, pose, super-resolution)
State of the art among autoregressive models on class-conditional ImageNet

method.summary: A VQGAN (conv encoder/decoder, learned codebook, perceptual + patch-GAN loss) compresses a 256x256 image to a 16x16 grid of indices; a GPT-2-style transformer models the index sequence autoregressively. Larger images are sampled with a sliding attention window.

datasets.name: ImageNet (IN) / Restricted ImageNet (RIN)
datasets.split: class-cond. FID against full training split, 50k samples
datasets.source: Deng et al.; RIN = animal subset (Santurkar et al.)
datasets.preprocessing: largest center-crop, bilinear resize with anti-aliasing to 256x256 (Pillow)

datasets.name: ADE20K, COCO-Stuff, S-FLCKR (Flickr landscapes with semantic layouts), DeepFashion, CIFAR-10
datasets.preprocessing: semantic layouts: first stage trained with cross-entropy reconstruction loss

models.name: VQGAN
models.architecture: conv encoder/decoder (ResNet blocks, GroupNorm, Swish, non-local/attention block at lowest resolution, no skip connections), patch discriminator
models.vocab: |Z|=1024 usually; 16384 for class-cond. ImageNet (973 used); 8192 COCO-Stuff; 4096 ADE20K

models.name: Transformer (GPT-2 architecture)
models.context: sequence length 256 typical (16x16); 512 or 257 (class token) in some

training.objective: VQGAN: perceptual reconstruction + codebook + commitment (beta=1.0, effective) + lambda*GAN with adaptive lambda = grad_L[Lrec]/(grad_L[LGAN]+delta); transformer: next-index negative log-likelihood
training.warmup: lambda (GAN weight) set to 0 in a warm-up phase; rule of thumb at least one epoch
training.batch_size: c-IN final model: 16 accumulated over 8 batches; others at least 2 per 12GB GPU
training.steps: c-IN final model 2.4 million steps (previous version 1.0 million)
training.hardware: generally 2-4 GPUs with 48GB accumulated VRAM; final c-IN model on a single A100
training.compute: final c-IN model 45.8 days on a single A100 GPU

other.commitment loss: paper v2 stated beta=0.25 but a bug meant beta=1.0 was used for all models; beta removed from Eq. 4
other.crop: transformer inputs cropped to 16x16 codes (16f x 16f pixels)

inference.decoding: top-k sampling (k=100 default, higher for larger codebooks); top-p and classifier rejection sampling for class-cond. ImageNet

parameters.rejection: ResNet-101 classifier keeps best m of n samples, acceptance rate m/n
parameters.sliding window: transformer applied over 16x16 code windows to sample beyond 256x256

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance, computed with torch-fidelity

metrics.name: NLL
metrics.definition: transformer negative log-likelihood of index sequence

eval.protocol: Single reported numbers, no seeds or confidence intervals stated (IS has +- values).

limits: Some task-specialised GANs report better FID (e.g. StyleGAN2 3.8 on FFHQ).
Sliding window assumes approximately spatially invariant statistics or spatial conditioning; unconditional aligned data needs coordinate conditioning.
Reconstruction quality bounds sample quality; f beyond a critical value (16 on faces) degrades.
Face model overfits the dataset; FID cannot detect it.
Comparisons in Table 4 use numbers from the papers, not re-evaluated, except BigGAN.
Optimizer, learning rate and schedule are not stated in the paper.

lineage.note: VQGAN replaces L2 loss by perceptual and adversarial
